props.code:
def command(key, name, category, inputs, outputs, doc):
    return {
        "key": key, "name": name, "category": category, "kind": "builtin",
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "required": list(inputs.keys()),
                         "properties": inputs, "additionalProperties": False},
        "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": outputs},
        "implementation": {"handler": key.replace(".", "_")},
        "required_permissions": ["commands.execute"],
        "required_capabilities": [],
        "timeout_ms": 10000, "risk_level": "low", "effect": "read",
        "trust_level": "trusted", "doc": doc,
    }

text_in = {"text": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 1048576}}
value_in = {"value": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 4096}}

def writing_command(key, name, inputs, outputs, doc):
    # Effect mutating, because these are the steps that produce something a
    # person sees. A dry run returns the example and writes nothing.
    definition = command(key, name, "Alert", inputs, outputs, doc)
    definition["effect"] = "mutating"
    definition["risk_level"] = "low"
    definition["required_capabilities"] = ["net"]
    definition["dry_run_example"] = {"dry_run": True, "would_call": key}
    return definition

def write_command(key, name, inputs, outputs, doc, required=None):
    # A command that changes platform state rather than calling out. It
    # runs on a worker with a database handle and no credential lease,
    # which is why it is its own kind rather than a builtin: a builtin is
    # pure by definition and cannot be handed a connection.
    definition = command(key, name, "Alert", inputs, outputs, doc)
    definition["kind"] = "write"
    definition["effect"] = "mutating"
    definition["risk_level"] = "low"
    definition["dry_run_example"] = {"dry_run": True, "would_write": key}
    if required is not None:
        definition["input_schema"]["required"] = required
    return definition

def ai_command(key, name, inputs, outputs, doc, risk="low"):
    # Deliberately not a builtin: a builtin runs in-process, and a model
    # call is network I/O against a third party. This runs on a worker like
    # any other command that leaves the box.
    definition = command(key, name, "AI", inputs, outputs, doc)
    definition["kind"] = "ai"
    definition["required_capabilities"] = ["net"]
    definition["timeout_ms"] = 120000
    definition["risk_level"] = risk
    # ai.execute, not ai.use: running a prompt is an engineering act that
    # an analyst inherits by running the playbook, never by asking directly.
    definition["required_permissions"] = ["commands.execute"]
    return definition

prompt_in = {
    "prompt": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 32768},
    "context": {"type": "object"},
    "purpose": {"enum": ["triage", "summarise", "classify", "extract",
                         "draft"]},
    "model_role": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 64},
}

return [
    writing_command("alert.create", "Create the alert",
                    {"title": {"type": "string"},
                     "description": {"type": "string"},
                     "severity": {"type": "string"},
                     "source": {"type": "string"},
                     "entities": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
                     "indicators": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
                     "raw": {"type": "object"}},
                    {"alert_id": {"type": "string"},
                     "incident_id": {"type": "string"}},
                    "Write the alert the analyst queue shows, from whatever "
                    "the playbook decided it should say."),

    writing_command("notify.email", "Send an email",
                    {"to": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
                     "subject": {"type": "string"},
                     "body": {"type": "string"},
                     "format": {"enum": ["html", "text"]}},
                    {"sent": {"type": "boolean"},
                     "recipients": {"type": "integer"}},
                    "Email the client. A separate step from creating the "
                    "alert, so a playbook can do either, both, or neither - "
                    "which is what customers actually contract for."),

    ai_command("ai.prompt", "AI: Run Prompt", prompt_in,
               {"text": {"type": "string"},
                "structured": {"type": "object"},
                "model": {"type": "string"},
                "tokens_in": {"type": "integer"},
                "tokens_out": {"type": "integer"},
                "grounded_in": {"type": "array",
                                "items": {"type": "string"}}},
               "A prompt, rendered against whatever is wired into it. The "
               "context object is the playbook's own data - an alert, an "
               "indicator, a command output - and every field the answer "
               "rests on comes back in grounded_in, so a conclusion drawn "
               "from an attacker-controlled field is visible as such."),
    ai_command("ai.classify", "AI: Classify", 
               {"prompt": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 8192},
                "context": {"type": "object"},
                "labels": {"type": "array",
                           "items": {"type": "string"}}},
               {"label": {"type": "string"},
                "confidence": {"type": "number"},
                "rationale": {"type": "string"}},
               "Choose one of the labels the playbook supplies. Constrained "
               "output, because a free-text answer that a switch node has "
               "to parse is a branch decided by prose."),
    write_command("alert.add_panel", "Alert: Add Detail Panel",
                  {"alert_id": {"type": "string"},
                   "key": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 64},
                   "title": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 120},
                   "fields": {"type": "array", "maxItems": 60,
                              "items": {"type": "object"}},
                   "body": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 16384},
                   "placement": {"enum": ["side", "main"]},
                   "sort_order": {"type": "integer"}},
                  {"panel_id": {"type": "string"}},
                  "Add a titled block of fields to an alert, from the "
                  "playbook that already runs for this client and this "
                  "tool. fields is a list of {label, value, kind} - kind "
                  "may be text, code, link or indicator. body is a small "
                  "markup subset (p, b, i, code, ul, li, a, br) rendered "
                  "as nodes, never as innerHTML: a panel can carry values "
                  "lifted from a vendor payload, and that is the one place "
                  "raw HTML must not reach.",
                  required=["alert_id", "key", "title"]),

    command("alert.severity", "Decide severity", "Alert",
            {"raw_severity": {"type": "string"},
             "severity_map": {"type": "object"},
             "default_severity": {"enum": ["critical", "high", "medium",
                                           "low", "info"]}},
            {"severity": {"type": "string"},
             "mapped": {"type": "boolean"}},
            "Translate the vendor's word for severity into ours. The map is "
            "the client's, because two customers of the same SOC do not "
            "agree on what high means."),

    command("alert.should_close", "Should this close?", "Alert",
            {"alert": {"type": "object"},
             "rules": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"close": {"type": "boolean"},
             "matched": {"type": "string"}},
            "Evaluate the client's auto-close rules against one alert. "
            "Returns WHICH rule matched, so an analyst asking why an alert "
            "closed itself gets an answer rather than a shrug."),

    command("alert.render", "Render description", "Alert",
            {"template": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 65536},
             "context": {"type": "object"},
             "format": {"enum": ["html", "text"]}},
            {"rendered": {"type": "string"},
             "format": {"type": "string"}},
            "Build what an analyst reads, from a template the engineer "
            "wrote. The same path resolver the rest of the platform uses, "
            "so a template cannot reach a Python attribute or a builtin."),

    command("ioc.extract", "Extract IOCs", "IOC", text_in,
            {"indicators": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
             "count": {"type": "integer"}},
            "Pull observables out of free text, refanged and deduplicated."),
    command("ioc.detect_type", "Detect IOC Type", "IOC", value_in,
            {"type": {"type": "string"}},
            "Classify one observable."),
    command("ioc.normalise", "Normalise IOC", "IOC", value_in,
            {"normalised": {"type": "string"}, "type": {"type": "string"}},
            "Canonical form, which is the global deduplication key."),
    command("ioc.defang", "Defang", "IOC", value_in,
            {"defanged": {"type": "string"}},
            "Make an indicator safe to paste into a ticket."),
    command("ioc.refang", "Refang", "IOC", value_in,
            {"refanged": {"type": "string"}},
            "The inverse of defang."),
    command("net.dns_lookup", "DNS Lookup", "Network",
            {"domain": {"type": "string"},
             "record": {"enum": ["A", "AAAA", "MX", "TXT", "NS", "CNAME"]}},
            {"records": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            "Forward DNS resolution."),
    command("net.reverse_dns", "Reverse DNS", "Network",
            {"ip": {"type": "string"}},
            {"hostnames": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            "PTR lookup."),
    command("net.whois", "WHOIS", "Network",
            {"target": {"type": "string"}},
            {"registrar": {"type": "string"}, "created": {"type": "string"},
             "age_days": {"type": "integer"}, "raw": {"type": "string"}},
            "Registration detail. Domain age alone is a useful phishing signal."),
    command("data.transform", "Transform", "Data",
            {"input": {"type": "object"}, "mapping": {"type": "object"}},
            {"output": {"type": "object"}},
            "Reshape a structure using the same path syntax as the mappings."),
    command("intel.score", "Score Indicator", "Threat Intelligence",
            {"verdicts": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"score": {"type": "integer"}, "verdict": {"type": "string"}},
            "Weighted aggregate of provider verdicts."),
    command("mitre.parse", "Parse ATT&CK ID", "MITRE",
            {"raw": {"type": "string"}},
            {"technique": {"type": "string"}, "sub_technique": {"type": "string"},
             "valid": {"type": "boolean"}},
            "Split T1566.001 so coverage is not counted twice."),
]

Run a command that changes platform state.

Separate from dispatch_builtin because a builtin is pure - no database, no
network, no clock - and that purity is what makes running it inside the
worker process defensible. These need a connection, so they get one, and
they still get no credential lease because none of them leave the box.

props.code:
from soar.platform.ids import new_id

import json

if key == "alert.add_panel":
    alert_id = str(inputs["alert_id"])
    rows = db.query("SELECT id FROM alert WHERE id = %s AND org_id = %s",
                    [alert_id, org_id], org_id)
    if not rows:
        raise KeyError("no such alert in this client")

    # Only the shapes the renderer knows. A kind it has never heard of
    # would render as nothing, which is worse than being told at the
    # step that wrote it.
    allowed = ("text", "code", "link", "indicator")
    fields = []
    for entry in (inputs.get("fields") or [])[:60]:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        kind = str(entry.get("kind", "text"))
        if kind not in allowed:
            raise ValueError(
                "field kind %r is not one of %s" % (kind, ", ".join(allowed)))
        fields.append({
            "label": str(entry.get("label", ""))[:120],
            "value": str(entry.get("value", ""))[:4096],
            "kind": kind,
        })

    panel_id = new_id("apan")
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO alert_panel (id, org_id, alert_id, panel_key, title, "
        "fields, body, placement, sort_order, written_by) "
        "VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s) "
        "ON CONFLICT (alert_id, panel_key) DO UPDATE SET "
        "title = EXCLUDED.title, fields = EXCLUDED.fields, "
        "body = EXCLUDED.body, placement = EXCLUDED.placement, "
        "sort_order = EXCLUDED.sort_order",
        [panel_id, org_id, alert_id, str(inputs["key"])[:64],
         str(inputs["title"])[:120], json.dumps(fields),
         str(inputs.get("body", ""))[:16384],
         inputs.get("placement", "side"),
         int(inputs.get("sort_order", 100)), "playbook"],
        org_id)
    return {"panel_id": panel_id, "fields": len(fields)}

raise KeyError("no write handler for %r" % key)
